Rashi on Bava Metzia 28b:12:1.hebrew: אמרו ליה אין - כסבורין שאמר להן "ידעיתון ביה דלאו רמאי הוא?", שכך היה לו לשואלן:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 28b:12:1.english: They said to him, "Yes" - [They said this] thinking that he had said to them, "Do you know about him that he is not a swindler?" — for that is how he should have asked them.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 28b:12:2.hebrew: מסתברא - שזה היה דעתן מתחילה, ואין כאן משום מגיד וחוזר ומגיד:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 28b:12:2.english: It is reasonable - that this was their intention from the outset, and there is no [issue] here of [a witness] testifying and then retracting and testifying [again].

Rashi on Bava Metzia 28b:12:3.hebrew: לא מייתי איניש חובה לנפשיה - וכשהביאן לב"ד, בטוח היה שלא יעידו חובתו:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 28b:12:3.english: A person does not bring condemnation upon himself - And when he brought them to court, he was confident that they would not testify against him.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 28b:13:1.hebrew: כל דבר שעושה ואוכל - אם אבידה זו דבר שיכולין להאכילו את שכר מעשיו, כגון שור וחמור, יעשה ויאכל, ולא ימכור אותו המוצא אם שהו בעליו מלדרשו, שכל אדם נוח לו בבהמתו, שהכירה בו כבר ולימדה לרצונו:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 28b:13:1.english: Anything that works and eats - If this lost item [is] something that one can feed [with] the earnings of its labor, such as an ox or a donkey, it shall work and eat, and the finder shall not sell it if its owners delay in seeking it, for every person is content with his [own] animal, since it already recognizes him and he has trained it to his will.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 28b:13:2.hebrew: ראה היאך תשיבנו לו - שלא תאכילנו חצי דמיו, שא"כ אין זו השבה:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 28b:13:2.english: See how you shall return it to him - That you should not feed it [the cost of] half its value, for if so, this is not a return.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 28b:15:1.english: And forever - Is this [finder] obligated forever to trouble himself with the burden of guarding [it]?

Rashi on Bava Metzia 28b:15:2.english: [One] assesses their value - [He] sells them and leaves the money with himself.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 28b:16:1.english: Calves and foals - Small [animals] that do not perform labor.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 28b:16:2.english: Roosters - Males, which do not lay eggs.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 28b:17:1.hebrew: כבהמה גסה - שעושה ואוכלת, ומטפל בה י"ב חדש, דיכול להאכילה דמי בצים:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 28b:17:1.english: Like a large domesticated animal - For it produces and eats, and [one] tends to it [for] twelve months, since he can feed it [with] the value of [its] eggs.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 28b:17:2.english: He tends to [them] - *Ensemètre* [to occupy oneself with / attend to] in Old French.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 28b:19:1.hebrew: הא דרעיא הא דפטומא - הא דקתני שלשה [חדשים], בארץ מרעה ובזמן הדשאים, שאין טיפולו מרובה. והא דקתני ל' [יום], בזמן שאין מרעה, וצריך לפטמה על אבוסה ממה שבבית, שדמיה יקרים:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 28b:19:1.english: This [refers to] grazing, [and] that [refers to] fattening - That [baraita] which teaches three [months] [refers to] a pasture land and a time of grasses, when its care is not extensive. And that [baraita] which teaches thirty [days] [refers to] a time when there is no pasture, and one must fatten it at its trough from what is in the house, whose cost is high.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 28b:1:1.english: (It comes to be confused with the second - perhaps there is [someone] who thinks that he said "second Festival".)

Rashi on Bava Metzia 28b:20:1.hebrew: רברבי - אוכלין הרבה, הלכך ג' ימים, דהא אוקימנא בזכרים:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 28b:20:1.english: Large [ones] - They eat a lot; therefore, [the finder keeps them for] three days, for we have already established [that it refers] to males.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 28b:21:1.hebrew: שלא יאכיל עגל לעגלים - מן העגלים שנמצא, לא יאכיל לו דמי עגל:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 28b:21:1.english: That he shall not feed a calf to calves - From the calves that were found, he shall not feed it the value of a calf.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 28b:22:1.english: They only disagree - With regard to becoming liable for its loss.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 28b:3:1.english: Udya of dinars - A vessel full of gold coins.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 28b:4:1.english: And this is [what] we learned - In Tractate Ta'anit (19a), [in the passage] concerning Choni HaMe'agel.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 28b:4:2.hebrew: צאו וראו אם נמחת אבן טוען - אם נכסת בגשמים, שגבהו הגשמים למעלה הימנו ויש גשמים יותר מדאי, ואתפלל עליהם שילכו:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 28b:4:2.english: Go and see if the Claimant's Stone has been obscured - If it has been covered by the rains, [meaning] that the rains have risen above it and there is too much rain, and I will pray for them to go away.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 28b:7:1.hebrew: חיישינן לרמאי - שמא שמע האובד מתאונן בין שכיניו: "טליתי נאבדה", וזה יודע את סימניה; וכשישמע את מוצאה מכריז: "טלית מצאתי", יקום ויתן סימניה. הלכך, אבידתא מכריז, ואינו נותן לב לומר: "טלית זו אבדתי ואלו סימניה":
Rashi on Bava Metzia 28b:7:1.english: We are concerned about a swindler - Perhaps [the swindler] heard the one who lost [it] complaining among his neighbors, "My cloak was lost," and this [swindler] knows its distinguishing marks; and when he hears its finder proclaiming, "I found a cloak," he will arise and state its distinguishing marks. Therefore, [the finder] proclaims "a lost item," and [the swindler] does not think to say, "I lost this cloak, and these are its distinguishing marks."

Rashi on Bava Metzia 28b:8:1.hebrew: אין לדבר סוף - דהשתא נמי מסיק אדעתיה ואמר, "אם טלית היא שמצאת, אלו סימניה":
Rashi on Bava Metzia 28b:8:1.english: There is no end to the matter - For even now, [the swindler] could bring it to mind and say, "If it is a cloak that you found, these are its identifying marks."

Rashi on Bava Metzia 28b:9:1.hebrew: אי אמרת בשלמא אבידתא מכריז - ולא מזכיר שם החפץ, אצטריך תנא לאשמועינן דאע"ג דאמר האי טלית אבדתי, צריך ליתן סימנין:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 28b:9:1.english: Granted, if you say [he] proclaims "a lost item" - and does not mention the name of the object, it was necessary for the Tanna to teach us that even though [the claimant] says, "I lost this cloak," he must give distinguishing marks.

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 28b:15:1.hebrew: שם דמיהן - לקמן גבי עסקא דרב ספרא, אפרש בע"ה:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 28b:15:1.english: One assesses their value - Later, regarding Rav Safra's business venture [iska], I will explain [this], with God's help.

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 28b:22:1.hebrew: עד כאן לא פליגי אלא בנשתמש בהן - לאו דוקא "נשתמש", דאם נשתמש — לר"ע נמי חייב באחריותן; כיון דלדידיה אסור להשתמש, א"כ הוי שולח יד בפקדון, ואפילו החזיר — אין בכך כלום, דהא ר"ע סבר בפרק המפקיד (לקמן בבא מציעא דף מג:) דבעינן דעת בעלים. אלא ודאי "נשתמש" לאו דוקא, כדפרישית, אלא בשכר שמוש שמותר להשתמש קאמר, דלרבי טרפון, דאית ליה דמותר להשתמש, חייב באחריותן, דבההוא הנאה דאי מיתרמי ליה זבינא שקיל להו וזבין בהו — הוי עלייהו שומר שכר; ולר"ע, דאסור להשתמש בהן — פטור. אבל אם לא היה מותר להשתמש, היה פטור לכ"ע, והיינו כרבה:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 28b:22:1.english: They only disagree where he used them - [This does] not literally [mean] "he used [them]," for if he [actually] used [them], according to Rabbi Akiva he would also be liable for their responsibility; since according to him it is forbidden to use [them], if so, he is [considered] one who lays a hand on a deposit, and even if he returned [them], that is of no avail, for Rabbi Akiva holds in the chapter [entitled] HaMafkid (below, Bava Metzia 43b) that we require the owner's knowledge. Rather, certainly "he used [them]" is not literal, as I explained, but rather it means [that they disagree] regarding the benefit of use — that it is permitted to use [them] — for according to Rabbi Tarfon, who holds that it is permitted to use [them], he is liable for their responsibility, because through that benefit — that if a purchase happens to come his way, he takes them and buys with them — he becomes a paid bailee over them; whereas according to Rabbi Akiva, [who holds] that it is forbidden to use them, he is exempt. But if it were not permitted to use [them], he would be exempt according to everyone, and this is in accordance with Rabbah.

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 28b:4:1.hebrew: אבן טוען - מפרש בירושלמי: כשם שהאבן אינה יכולה למחות, כך אין יכולים להתפלל על רוב טובה:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 28b:4:1.english: Claimant’s Stone - [It] is explained in the Jerusalem Talmud: Just as the stone cannot be obliterated, so too they cannot pray against an excess of good.
